m: Om. I worship the auspicious Goddess, shining like the orb of the newly risen sun, four-armed and three-eyed,
holding the noose, the goad, the gesture of granting a boon, and the gesture of fearlessness. Om. The seer said:
King, I have told you this supreme glory of the Goddess. Such is the majesty of the Goddess by whom this world is upheld.
Knowledge, too, is brought about by her, the blessed Vishnu-maya. By her, you, this merchant, and other discerning people
are bewildered; those already bewildered remain so, and others will yet enter delusion. Great king, go to her for refuge, the supreme sovereign.
Worshipped, she herself gives human beings enjoyment, heaven, and final release.
Markandeya said:
Hearing his words, Suratha, that lord of men,
bowed to that fortunate sage of strict vows. Disillusioned by excessive attachment, and by the loss of his kingdom,
he went at once to practise austerity, and so did the merchant, great sage. He settled on a riverbank in order to see the Mother.
The merchant also practised austerity, reciting the supreme hymn of the Goddess. On that bank the two of them made an earthen image of the Goddess
and worshipped her with flowers, incense, fire, and water-offerings. They went without food, restrained themselves, kept their minds on her, and remained collected.
They also offered a bali moistened with blood from their own limbs. Worshipping her together in this way, self-restrained, for three years,
Chandika, supporter of the world, was pleased, and she spoke to them in person.
The Goddess said:
Whatever you ask, O king, and you, O joy of your family, receive all of it from me. I am pleased, and I give it to you.
Markandeya said:
The king then chose a kingdom that would not fall from him in another birth, and, in this life itself, his own kingdom, with the armies of his enemies destroyed by his strength.
The merchant, his mind disillusioned, then chose knowledge, he the wise one, knowledge that cuts away the attachments of mine and I.
The Goddess said:
In a few days, O king, you will obtain your own kingdom.
Having slain your enemies, it will be yours there without a fall.
And when you die, you will be born again through the god Vivasvat, the sun.
On earth you will be the Manu named Savarnika.
Best of merchants, the boon you desired from me —
I grant it for your fulfillment. Knowledge will be yours.
Markandeya said:
Having given each of them the boon he longed for, the Goddess,
praised by the devotion of those two, vanished at once. Having received the Goddess's boon in this way, Suratha, bull among kshatriyas,
will take birth from the sun and become the Manu Savarni.
